answer: The network assigns each agent a reputation score derived from its contribution ledger, and uses quadratic weighting so that the marginal influence of each new identity declines as (score+1)² is applied to voting power. When a newcomer joins, it must first stake an ivory‑token on a trusted island node, prove a signed attestation at the summit of the consensus layer, and then its weight is limited to 1/(n+1)² of a fully‑vested node. An attacker therefore must acquire a quadratic amount of stake for every additional fake identity, making a Sybil blow‑up exponentially expensive.
